newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former judge may bid for Hong Kong 1997 leadership.
newsitem.headline: Former judge may bid for Hong Kong 1997 leadership.

text.p: A former Hong Kong High Court judge said on Wednesday that he was considering a bid for the territory's leadership after Britain hands the colony back to China in the middle of next year.

Arthur Garcia told Hong Kong radio that he was actively considering running for the post of chief executive of Hong Kong after it becomes an autonomous Special Administrative Region of China at midnight on June 30, 1996.
"I think I have sufficient experience from all my work, in so far as I have known for some time how government machinery works," said Garcia, also a former civil servant.
Garcia, who has a Chinese mother and an Eurasian father, is presently a member of China's handpicked Preparatory Committee, which is working on the handover arrangements.
His statement came a week after the man considered the front runner for the post, shipping billionaire Tung Chee-hwa, said he was seriously considering standing.
Two other self-declared candidates are former Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang, and lawyer Lo Tak-shing.
Hong Kong's next leader, who will succeed the departing colonial Governor Chris Patten, will be chosen by a 400-member, China-controlled Selection Committee, to be formed in November.
